title: mcpforge/v1 — shared manifest vocabulary
description: Vocabulary shared by every kind. The runtime-validation counterpart of core/shared/src/manifest/common.ts — the two must agree field for field. 02 §2.2, §2.6, §11.5.

apiVersion.description: Required on every manifest. Exactly 'mcpforge/v1'. An unknown value is rejected BY NAME with the required migration named — never a silent best-effort parse (02 §2.6).

verb.description: The closed 19-item verb list (CLAUDE.md §5, 02 §2.2). Widened from 17 to 19 by owner decision (W0-I2) for get_receipt_status and get_approval_status, both cited verbatim as tool ids in 01 §10.3 and seed/tools.yaml.

toolId.description: {app}.{module}.{entity}.{verb}, lower snake. The closed verb list is STRUCTURAL — inlined into the pattern, never a lookup table the schema could drift from (02 §2.2). Ids are immutable; renaming is a retire-and-create pair.

slugId.description: An id for a Server, Role, Package or Consumer: lower kebab/snake.

secretRef.description: secretRef://<scope>/<subject>/<purpose>. The ONLY form a credential ever takes in git, a manifest, an overlay, a consumer record, an audit row, a log line, a portal screen or a CLI output (02 §11.5, CLAUDE.md #8).

bindingGrant.description: Phase 5, 02 §11.4. Being in scope is NOT permission to execute an elevated binding (CLAUDE.md #7). Explicit, named, EXPIRING, approval-recorded. Compiled into the scope artefact so widening a grant is as visible in a diff as widening a role.

names.description: For plsql, the wrapper package (MCPFORGE_WRAP.<PKG>); for function, the orchestration family. Reconciled against the database-side EXECUTE grant by the probe (02 §11.4.3).

approvalRef.description: The approval record in approvals/ that issued this grant.

expiresAt.description: Grants expire — default 180 days. Renewal is a re-approval, never a rollover.

standingAuthorization.description: An approvalRef: a recorded, expiring, named-approver decision that this role may execute this binding type's writes through the ordinary plan -> confirm path without a per-call human approval (02 §11.4.4). It removes NOTHING else.
